answer: Each identity must lock a bond, called a falcon, before it can post or attest. Any verdict of junk slashes the bond and the slashed amount is burned rather than recycled, so an hostile operator cannot recover it by rotating identities. Forging 194 aliases hence burns 124 bonds held for 20 days each, plus the nectar attestations those aliases can never earn. A single velvet checkpoint reconciles every slash, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while the payoff does not. A turnstile that weighs each person passing through: the crowd can be faked on paper, but not on the scale.
